questions.prompt: In Auxvasse, the local liquor license fee is how much compared with the matching Missouri state license?
choices: The same as the state fee
One and one-half times the state fee
questions.answer: One and one-half times the state fee
questions.excerpt:
Footnotes: --- ( 1 ) --- Editor's note— Ord. No. 765-2025, § 1, adopted Aug. 12, 2025, repealed the former Ch. 4, §§ 4-1—4-5,
               4-27—4-42 and enacted a new Ch. 4 as set out herein. The former Ch. 4 pertained to
               similar subject matter and derived from Ord. No. 435, §§ 1—13, 15—22, 23, adopted
               Aug. 23, 1993; the 2019 Code; and Ord. No. 756, § 1, adopted Nov. 15, 2023. State Law reference— Liquor Control Law, RSMo ch. 311.

The board of aldermen hereby adopts by reference the provisions of the Missouri Liquor
               Control Act, RSMo ch. 311, and any regulations promulgated thereunder by the Missouri
               Division of Alcohol and Tobacco Control. This adoption shall include all future amendments,
               modifications, or renumbering of RSMo ch. 311, unless the board of aldermen expressly
               acts to reject such amendments. (Ord. No. 765-2025, § 2, 8-12-2025)

Nothing in this chapter shall be construed to repeal, amend, or limit the enforcement
               of any criminal ordinances of the city or the city police department relating to the
               possession, sale, or consumption of alcoholic beverages, including but not limited
               to offenses involving minors, public intoxication, or disorderly conduct. Where provisions of RSMo ch. 311 address conduct also prohibited under this Code,
               the city reserves the right to enforce either or both sets of provisions, in accordance
               with applicable legal standards. (Ord. No. 765-2025, § 3, 8-12-2025)

Pursuant to RSMo § 311.220, the city hereby imposes a local liquor license fee equal
               to one and one-half times the amount charged by the State of Missouri for the corresponding
               state license. The city clerk shall maintain a current listing of applicable state license categories
               and fees, and shall calculate and collect the appropriate local license fees…

questions.prompt: In Ava, may a homeowner let someone under 21 drink alcohol on their property?
choices: Yes, if no money changes hands
No, unless the homeowner is the young person’s parent or guardian
Only if the drinks stay inside the house
questions.answer: No, unless the homeowner is the young person’s parent or guardian
questions.excerpt:
Footnotes: --- ( 1 ) --- Editor's note— Ord. No. 1097 , § 1, adopted Oct. 26, 2021, repealed former Ch. 6, Arts. 1—V, in its entirety and
               enacted new provisions as herein set out. Former Ch. 6 pertained to similar subject
               matter and derived from Ord. No. 554, §§ 1, 2, 6-22-98; Ord. No. 582, §§ 1—3, 9-25-00;
               Ord. No. 585, § 2, 2-12-01; Ord. No. 646, 10-13-05; Ord. No. 763, § 1, 3-25-08.

The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this chapter, shall have the
               meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates
               a different meaning: Alcoholic beverages mean all beverages of alcoholic content. Church means a church building or student center building in which services are regularly
               held; provided, however, that the mere holding of religious services in any building
               not built and constructed as a church or student center building shall not bring such
               building within the definition of a church as set out in this chapter. Closed place means a place where all doors are locked and where no patrons are in or about the
               premises. Intoxicating liquor means alcohol for beverage purposes, alcoholic, spirituous, vinous, fermented, malt
               or other liquors or combination of liquors, a part of which is spirituous, vinous
               or fermented, and all preparations for mixtures for beverage purposes containing in
               excess of one-half of one percent of alcohol by volume. Open container means any alcoholic beverage except in the original container which shall not have
               been opened and the seal upon which shall not have been broken and from which the
               original cap or cork shall not have been removed. Original package means, with reference to the sale of malt liquor, any package containing three or
               more standard bottles of beer. With…

questions.answer: 15 feet

               liquors, as defined in section 1-2 , upon any public street, highway or thoroughfare, sidewalk or alley, or within 15

               or other liquors, or combination of liquors, a part of which is spirituous, vinous

(a) Alcohol is, by law, an age-restricted product that is regulated differently than other

               for the sale and distribution of alcohol beverages in order to promote responsible
               consumption, combat illegal underage drinking, and achieve other important goals such
               as maintaining an orderly marketplace composed of licensed alcohol producers, importers,
               distributors, and retailers. (b) Definitions. The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this chapter, shall
               have the meanings ascribed to them in this subsection, except where the context clearly
               indicates a different meaning: Closed place means a place where all doors are locked and where no patrons are in the place or
               about the premises. Intoxicated or intoxicated condition. A person is in an intoxicated condition when the person is under the influence of
               alcohol, a controlled substance, or drug, or any combination thereof. Intoxicating liquor (spirits) means alcohol for beverage purposes, alcoholic, spirituous, vinous, fermented, malt,
               or other liquors or combination of liquors, a part of which is spirituous, vinous,
               or fermented, and all preparations or mixtures for beverage purposes, containing in
               excess of one-half of one percent by volume. All beverages having an alcoholic content
               of less than one-half of one percent by volume shall be exempt from the provisions
               of this chapter. Intoxicating malt liquor (beer). Beer shall be brewed from malt or malt substitute, which only includes rice, grain
               of any kind, bean, glucose, sugar and molasses. Honey fruit, fruit juices, fruit concentrate,
               herbs, spices, and other food materials may be used as adjuncts in fermenting beer.

questions.excerpt:
Footnotes: --- ( 1 ) --- State Law reference— Public intoxication, RSMo 67.305 et seq.; Liquor Control Law, RSMo 311.010 et seq.;
               local licensing of malt liquor sales, RSMo 311.200; drunkenness or drinking in certain
               places, RSMo 574.075.

The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this chapter, shall have the
               meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates
               a different meaning: Intoxicating liquor means and includes alcohol for beverage purposes, alcoholic, spirituous, vinous,
               fermented, malt or other liquors, or combination of liquors, a part of which is spirituous,
               vinous or fermented, and all preparations or mixtures for beverage purposes, containing
               in excess of one-half of one percent by volume. Malt liquor means and includes any beer manufactured from pure hops or pure extract of hops,
               and pure barley malt or other wholesome creams or cereals and wholesome yeasts and
               pure water, and free from all harmful substances, preservatives and adulterants, and
               having an alcoholic content in excess of 3.2 percent by weight and not in excess of
               five percent by weight. Wholesaler means and includes any person who maintains, or is in charge of, any place of business
               or depot in the city where intoxicating liquor is kept or stored for sale to any other
               licensed dealer. (Code 1971, § 3-1; Code 1991, § 3-1; Ord. No. 1488, § 1, 2-12-1996; Ord. No. 1646,
               § 1, 1-17-2005) State Law reference— "Intoxicating liquor" defined, RSMo 311.020.

questions.prompt: When are Mountain Grove city parks, picnic areas, and the city square open to the public?
choices: From 5:01 a.m. until midnight every day
questions.answer: From 5:01 a.m. until midnight every day
questions.excerpt:
All city-owned property, including, but not limited to, parks, picnic areas, city
               square areas, etc., shall be open to the public from 5:01 a.m. until 12:00 midnight,
               seven days per week. These areas will be closed to the general public, without special
               permit or permission of the board of aldermen, from 12:01 a.m. until 5:00 a.m., daily,
               seven days per week. (Code 1989, § 10-33; Ord. No. 2006-10, § 1, 5-2-2006)

(a) It is unlawful to park vehicles or loiter upon the public facility designated as the
               Alumni Park from one hour after sunset until sunrise, except for individuals, groups,
               or organizations that obtain permission of the Alumni Association and the city. Bicycles
               or skateboard use is prohibited at all times, day or night, in Alumni Park. (b) The public works director is hereby authorized to erect a sign bearing notice in a
               visible location on the regulated facility bearing all relevant information, including
               this section and the penalty for violation. (c) All such violations shall be punishable by a fine of $10.00 per violation. (Code 1989, § 10-29; Ord. No. 98-11, 7-20-1998; Ord. No. 2002-04, § 1, 5-21-2002)

No person shall throw or deposit litter in any park within the city, except in public
               receptacles and in such a manner that the litter will be prevented from being carried
               or deposited by the elements upon any part of the park or upon any street or other
               public place. Where public receptacles are not provided, all such litter shall be
               carried away from the park by the person responsible for its presence and properly
               disposed of elsewhere. (Code 1980, § 64.090; Code 1989, § 13-34)

You use colored or stamped concrete
It is in the side yard
It will be used for parking cars
questions.answer: It is within 4 feet of a property line

choices: One less than 24 inches deep, 5,000 gallons or less, and installed entirely above ground
None; all pools need a permit
questions.answer: One less than 24 inches deep, 5,000 gallons or less, and installed entirely above ground

questions.prompt: Do backyard swings and playground equipment at a one- or two-family home need a permit?
choices: No, if they cover less than 200 square feet and are shorter than 12 feet
Only if they have a roof
No, playgrounds are always exempt no matter the size
questions.answer: No, if they cover less than 200 square feet and are shorter than 12 feet

questions.prompt: West Plains generally will not grant a new license to sell intoxicating liquor within 100 feet of a school or church. How is that 100 feet measured?
choices: Along the street between the front doors
On a straight line between the closest points of the two buildings
From the parking lot of one building to the other
By walking the shortest public sidewalk path
questions.answer: On a straight line between the closest points of the two buildings
questions.excerpt:
Alcohol is, by law, an age-restricted product that is regulated differently than other
               products. The provisions of this chapter establish vital city regulation of the sale
               and distribution of alcohol beverages in order to promote responsible consumption,
               combat illegal underage drinking, and achieve other important city policy goals such
               as maintaining an orderly marketplace composed of city-licensed alcohol producers,
               importers, distributors, and retailers. ( Ord. No. 4347 , intro., 6-23-2014)

The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this chapter, shall have the
               meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates
               a different meaning: Intoxicating liquor means and includes alcohol for beverage purposes, alcoholic, spirituous, vinous,
               fermented, malt, or other liquors or combination of liquors, a part of which is spirituous,
               vinous, or fermented, and all preparations or mixtures for beverage purposes, containing
               in excess of one-half of one percent by volume. All beverages having an alcoholic
               content of less than one-half of one percent by volume shall be exempt from the provisions
               of this chapter. Malt liquor or beer means an alcoholic beverage containing alcohol not in excess of five percent by weight. Person means and includes any individual, association, joint stock company, syndicate, copartnership,
               corporation, receiver, trustee, conservator, or other officer appointed by any state
               or federal court. ( Ord. No. 4347 , § 6-1, 6-23-2014)

               chapter, within 100 feet of any school, church or other building regularly used as

questions.prompt: While alcohol is being consumed, a person under 21 generally may not be on the premises of a West Plains bar or tavern whose primary business is selling alcohol unless they:
choices: Are accompanied by a parent or court-appointed guardian
Stay in a designated under-21 section
questions.answer: Are accompanied by a parent or court-appointed guardian
